thm:main.statement: The prescribed lazy four-vertex switch chain mixes to total variation 1/4 within 2 n^8 steps for every graphical labelled degree vector.
thm:main.conditions: n>=4; all simple undirected realizations on the complete labelled vertex set; no additional constraints.
thm:main.constants_and_limits: For M>1, gap>=1/[24 n^2 C(n,4)]. Off-diagonal neighbor probability 1/[12 C(n,4)], not the arbitrary accepted-switch chain. Singleton mixes at time zero.

cor:exact-sampling.statement: Exactly uniform graph sampler using unbiased bits terminates almost surely with expected polynomial bit cost in the explicit degree-vector encoding length.
cor:exact-sampling.conditions: Input graphical finite labelled degree vector; small n enumerated separately; complete unrestricted simple undirected state space.
cor:exact-sampling.constants_and_limits: Rare residual branch enumerates exponentially many graphs and transition entries. Expected polynomial cost gives no worst-case latency or memory guarantee; exact sampler is outside selected Lean scope.

row:fixed-blocks.statement: Variance of a sum of three arbitrary row-block functions is at most twice the sum of their variances.
row:fixed-blocks.conditions: Independent uniform ordered partitions of two finite labelled sets, with all six block sizes fixed.
row:fixed-blocks.constants_and_limits: Factor 2 is an upper budget, not row independence or universal negative covariance. Fixed-size conditional partitions required.

row:counts.statement: Variance of sum_i b_i(X_i) is at most 2 sum_i Var b_i(X_i) for arbitrary real coordinate functions.
row:counts.conditions: X>=0, sum X=m; probability proportional to product_i 1/[X_i!(X_i+alpha_i)!], all alpha_i,m nonnegative integers.
row:counts.constants_and_limits: Adjacent-total sandwich coupling and spectral argument. This special product-conditioned law is essential; old FQW26 Lemma5.3 already supplies the count-sector gap.

row:variance.statement: Variance of a sum of arbitrary three binary-row functions is at most twice their marginal variance sum.
row:variance.conditions: Uniform distribution on the nonempty full set of three-row binary matrices with fixed row and column margins.
row:variance.constants_and_limits: Remove forced column sums0/3; condition on counts, independent partitions then total variance. Not arbitrary weighted matrices or symmetric adjacency matrices without further encoding.

tri:gap.statement: Each three-vertex conditional pair-resampling generator satisfies H_T^2 >= H_T.
tri:gap.conditions: Encode the full triple fiber as a three-row fixed-margin binary matrix with zero or one extra column.
tri:gap.constants_and_limits: Internal edge count 0,1,2,3 uses row shifts and an extra column for cases1/2. Extra coordinate must retain both internal-edge choices, not freeze an individual edge.

dis:interaction.statement: For disjoint pairs, 2<h_a f,h_b f> >=2||g_ab f||^2-||R_ab f||^2-||R_ba f||^2.
dis:interaction.conditions: Full graph-space pair fibers and actual cross-cell conditional laws; R are directed error-line projections.
dis:interaction.constants_and_limits: Disjoint pair projections need not commute; individual interaction may be negative. Cross total2 has a rank-one correlated plane; gain is a cross-toggle projection.

sl:comparison.statement: On a uniform Boolean slice, the sum of centered equality-indicator projections is bounded by the unnormalized transposition generator.
sl:comparison.conditions: N>=0, 0<=q<=N; Q_ij=0 for constant equality indicator; G=(1/2)sum_{i<j}(I-tau_ij).
sl:comparison.constants_and_limits: S<=G, including degenerate slices. Coefficient sectors C0/C1/C2 and Gram eigenvalues used; not a claim that equality indicators are independent.

sl:global.statement: For each pair a, sum of directed disjoint error energies is at most the sum of its cross-toggle gain energies.
sl:global.conditions: Apply the Boolean-slice operator comparison in each actual pair fiber, then average.
sl:global.constants_and_limits: Exact error-line localization and unordered indexing required; not pointwise domination of each error term.

dis:nonnegative.statement: The ordered sum of h_a h_b over disjoint pairs is self-adjoint and positive semidefinite.
dis:nonnegative.conditions: Aggregate the interaction lower bounds and the full fiberwise error budget.
dis:nonnegative.constants_and_limits: Only the total ordered sum is positive; individual products may be noncommuting and need not be positive.

mix:global.statement: The full unnormalized pair-resampling generator satisfies H^2 >= H.
mix:global.conditions: Triple-square bounds plus nonnegative aggregated disjoint interactions.
mix:global.constants_and_limits: H^2=sum_T H_T^2-(n-3)H+D; each pair belongs to n-2 triples. No unsupported disjoint commutation shortcut.

mix:connectivity.statement: All simple labelled realizations of a graphical degree vector are connected by valid switches.
mix:connectivity.conditions: Same nonempty full degree-vector state space.
mix:connectivity.constants_and_limits: Direct Havel greedy alignment with a fixed tie order and strictly improving retained neighbors, not connectivity of each graph as a graph.

mix:poincare.statement: The kernel of H is exactly constants and Var_pi(f)<=<f,Hf>.
mix:poincare.conditions: Switch connectivity and H^2>=H on the finite nonempty full state space.
mix:poincare.constants_and_limits: The pair resampling generator is not the discrete four-vertex transition matrix; a separate normalization and comparison are needed.

mix:comparison.statement: h_a<=n^2 J_a, sum_a J_a=2L, hence H<=2 n^2 L.
mix:comparison.conditions: J_a is the unnormalized transposition generator on the uniform pair fiber; L is the simple switch-graph Laplacian.
mix:comparison.constants_and_limits: Permutation paths use at most N transpositions; each distinct switch appears in exactly two opposite-pair trades. I-P=L/[12 C(n,4)].

quantifier_and_boundary_notes: For M>1, gap>=1/[24 n^2 C(n,4)]. Off-diagonal neighbor probability 1/[12 C(n,4)], not the arbitrary accepted-switch chain. Singleton mixes at time zero.

Natural main uses M<=2^C(n,2) and a tighter intermediate mixing time; selected Lean NumericMixing uses weaker M<=2^(n*n),sqrt(M)<=M and proves the same2n^8 final bound. Different proof estimates, not a discrepancy in the final specification.

Exact sampling proof: B=C(n,2),D=4B+10,delta=2^-D,t=ceil(gamma0^-1(B+2D+2)); TV<=delta^2 and Mdelta<=1 imply (1-delta)p_G<=1/M. Integer weights2^D q^t-M(2^D-1)a_G sum to Mq^t. Rare exponential cost is weighted bydelta; do not truncate the rare branch or bit rejection while claiming exact uniformity.

Caputo08.locator: Published2008, Section1.1, pp207-208, equations1.6-1.15; PDF text selected scope
Caputo08.scope: Squared-generator/triple decomposition uses disjoint commutation in that collision model. F131 must replace this step with a noncommuting interaction budget; no general disjoint positivity inferred.

CBS18.scope: Undirected trades include each switch twice. Practical motivation is stopping time; experiments modify the proposal and estimate mixing using perturbation-score stabilization. That statistic is not a full-law TV certificate.

CDG12.locator: 27March2012v1, abstract, introductory transition rule and Theorem1
CDG12.scope: Regular-graph bound corrected by d^8 to d^23 n^8(dn log(dn)+log(1/epsilon)). This corrects a proof bound, not a withdrawal. It uses an edge-pair kernel; normalize before comparing with F131.

Unified22.scope: Rapid mixing on P-stable families, including directed/bipartite variants. Explicit unconstrained off-diagonal probability1/[2 C(n,2) C(n-2,2)] equals1/[12 C(n,4)]. Scope remains P-stability rather than every graphical family.

FQW26.locator: 13July2026v2, Section5.1 Theorem5.1, Section5.2 Lemmas5.2/5.3 and count identification
FQW26.scope: Three-row projection/count inequalities already precede F131. Lemma5.3 gives gap>=1/3 for the same factorial count law; dual synthesis gives the factor2 variance budget. Bipartite matrix results do not alone cover symmetric undirected adjacency constraints.

GLMP2024.scope: Existing generic rare residual-mixture conversion requires target and approximate-output probabilities from expensive oracles. Expected cost weights the oracle cost by the rare probability. F131 supplies rational finite-state oracles and a graph-specific error budget, not a new generic conversion.

GS18.scope: With M=sum degrees, min degree>=1 and3<=max degree<=sqrt(M)/3, bound is maxdegree^14 M^9[(M/2)log M+log(1/epsilon)]. Earlier proof gap is repaired. Kernel/degree conditions cannot be silently dropped.
